findings.title: Time-based cleanup logs an `err` that is always nil at that point
findings.description: In the `cfg.MaxAge > 0` closure, `ids, err := r.fetchIDs(...)` is followed by `if err != nil { return 0, err }`. The next statement, `r.log.Error("Annotations to clean by time", ..., "err", err)`, therefore always logs `err: <nil>`. The field carries no information and should be removed, or the log should report the error that was actually returned.

findings.title: Tag cleanup logs an `err` that is always nil at that point
findings.description: Same slip as above. After `if err != nil { return 0, err }`, the `r.log.Error("Tags to clean", ..., "err", err)` call logs a nil error.

findings.title: Per-batch progress logs are emitted at Error level and include full ID lists
findings.description: Each batch in both `CleanAnnotations` branches and in `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags` calls `r.log.Error` twice. These are routine progress messages, not errors, so they will flood error logs on every cleanup cycle. The `"ids", ids` field can dump up to `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` IDs per line, and the cycle now runs every minute because of the ticker change in `cleanup.go`. These should be Debug-level (or removed), and the ID list should not be logged.

findings.title: `strings.Repeat` is used without a matching import in the shown hunk
findings.description: `deleteByIDs` calls `strings.Repeat`. The only import added in this diff is `sqlstore/migrator`. The `strings` package may already be imported elsewhere in the file, but I could not confirm that. If it is not, the file will not compile.

findings.title: Test case name refers to a limit the code does not use
findings.description: The case "should not fail if batch size is larger than SQLITE_MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER for SQLite >= 3.32.0" describes the SQLite 3.32+ limit. The implementation in `deleteByIDs` uses a hard-coded `sqliteParameterLimit = 999` and never checks the SQLite version. The name should match the threshold the code actually enforces.

findings.title: Unrelated change to the cleanup service ticker interval
findings.description: The ticker interval changes from 10 minutes to `time.Minute * 1`. This is not connected to the annotation fix, it is not explained in the diff, and it increases how often every cleanup job runs. `time.Minute * 1` can be written as `time.Minute`. If the change is intentional, it should be called out separately.
